paraphrase: Because some, lacking faith, place the sage's state beyond their reach and others, lacking wisdom, grow arrogant thinking themselves equal to the Buddha, one must know the six identities: identity in principle, verbal identity, identity in contemplative practice, identity of resemblance, identity of partial truth, and ultimate identity. They begin with the ordinary person and end with the sage: beginning with the ordinary removes doubt and timidity; ending with the sage removes arrogance.

original.text: 為此事故，須知六即，謂理即、名字即、觀行即、相似即、分真即、究竟即。此六即者，始凡終聖。始凡故，除疑怯；終聖故，除慢大。

paraphrase: The six identities explained: identity in principle — one moment of mind is the principle of the tathāgatagarbha (empty, provisional and middle), present in all; verbal identity — though principle is identical, in daily use one does not know it, until from a good friend or the sūtras one hears of the one real bodhi and understands in words that all dharmas are the buddha-dharma; identity in contemplative practice — mind and speech in accord, contemplation unceasing though not yet in accord with principle; identity of resemblance — the more one contemplates the clearer, like an archer nearing the target, as in the purification of the six senses, ignorance subdued and a wisdom resembling the middle way; identity of partial truth — through that power one enters the stage of the copper wheel, first breaks ignorance, sees the buddha-nature, opens the treasury and manifests suchness (the abode of arousing the mind), and so on up to equal awakening, manifesting bodies to save beings; ultimate identity — equal awakening turns into wondrous awakening, wisdom's light complete, nothing more to cut.

original.text: 理即者，一念心即如來藏理

paraphrase: The six identities in one simile: a poor man has a treasure in his house but does not know it; a knowing friend shows him and he knows; he clears the weeds and digs, gradually coming near; when near, the store is opened and he takes and uses it all.

original.text: 譬如貧人，家有寶藏而無知者，知識示之，即得知也；耘除草穢而掘出之，漸漸得近；近已藏開，盡取用之。
